verdicts.reason: A has a sensible left-to-right flow (logo and cards, then the headline with the CTA, then the subcopy), but the three fare cards are tiny, so the city names and 'from' labels can't be read. The logo is very small and the subcopy is wrapped into a cramped four-line block against the right edge. B breaks the structure: the cards are split and out of order (Reykjavik/$139 first, then $89 and $119 on the right), the logo sits under the CTA in the middle, the $89 card looks cut off or overlapped, the CTA is pushed to the top edge, and the subcopy is wrapped one or two words per line into an unreadable sliver.
